title: agentHost: discover external Copilot sessions
body:
## Problem

Copilot sessions created outside the Agent Host never appeared in the Agents window, even with `chat.agentHost.showExternalSessions` set to `all`.

`CopilotAgent` had a single discovery path, `_discoverExtHostChats()`, which:

1. only matched **legacy VS Code extension-host** CLI sessions, via a `~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/vscode.metadata.json` sidecar with `origin === 'vscode'`;
2. hard-coded `external: false` on everything it emitted;
3. was gated entirely behind `chat.agentHost.migrateLegacyCopilotCli.enabled`.

A session created by the standalone `copilot` CLI or the GitHub Copilot app — which all share `~/.copilot` — has no such marker, so it was dropped at step 1 and never reached `AgentService._registerDiscoveredChats`. The registry therefore never held a Copilot row with `external = true`, and the setting had nothing to filter.

Claude (`_emitClaudeCodeChats`) and Codex (`_emitCodexChats`) both emit every unknown native chat as `external: true`. Copilot was the outlier, and `AGENTS.md` §3a documented the gap as intentional.

## Change

`_discoverCopilotChats()` / `_emitCopilotChats()` enumerate the whole SDK catalog and classify each chat Agent Host does not already own:

- **legacy extension-host chat** → `external: false` + `ehcliAdoptable` meta, still gated on migrate-legacy (unchanged behavior);
- **anything else** → `external: true`, ungated.

"Already owns" is the presence of a per-session database under `{userDataPath}/agentSessionData` (never the shared Copilot home), which also keeps peer-chat backings out of the payload. Subagent sessions and marked chat backings are filtered centrally by `AgentService` as before.

Discovery now starts on first-listener attach behind a `retry` wrapper, mirroring Claude and Codex, so a cold CLI client doesn't lose the pass. The retry honors the file's existing `_shutdownPromise` / `_store.isDisposed` guard so teardown stops it rather than sleeping on a dead client.

Chats whose SDK context carries no working directory are still dropped. `_doResumeSession` requires one unconditionally and a discovered chat has no other source for it — `_initializeExternalSessionReadState` writes only `agentHost.isRead` — so surfacing one would list fine and then throw on open, with a plain `Error` rather than the `SessionWorkingDirectoryMissingError` the UI handles gracefully.

## Logging

A session that was discovered but filtered out by the setting was previously indistinguishable from one that was never discovered. The pipeline is now traceable end to end at `info`:

```
[Copilot] Listed N SDK session(s) for <reason>
[Copilot] Chat discovery: N SDK session(s) -> X external, Y adoptable legacy extension-host, Z already known to Agent Host, W without a working directory
[Copilot] Chat discovery: emitting X of Y discovered chat(s) (adopt legacy extension-host chats: <bool>)
[AgentService] discovery for provider <id>: N candidate(s) (X external), Y registered, Z suppressed as subagent/chat backing
[AgentService] listSessions hid N of M session(s) (showExternalSessions: '<mode>')
```

The last line is deduped on `hidden/total/mode` so a steady state logs once instead of on every refresh. All lines carry only counts, a mode name and session URIs — no file paths, summaries or user content.

## Notes

- `_registerDiscoveredChats` now computes its return value from a counter instead of `results.some(...)`. Semantically identical (booleans only); the value has no consumer today.
- The "empty session DB counts as known" semantics of `_readStoredSessionMetadata` are deliberately left alone — an empty DB is how Agent Host records a chat it already touched, and the pre-existing test `does not discover an extension-host chat with an empty Agent Host database` asserts exactly that. The trade-off is now written down in `AGENTS.md` rather than silently relied upon.

## Testing

Four new tests in a `external chat discovery` suite cover the standalone-CLI, GitHub-Copilot-app (`origin: 'other'`), adoptable-legacy, and already-owned / no-working-directory cases. `writeExtensionHostMarker` was hoisted out of the nested migration suite so both suites share it.

- `copilotAgent.test.ts` — 267 passing (3 consecutive runs)
- `agentService.test.ts` — 290 passing
- `tsc --project src/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — clean apart from two pre-existing `@github/copilot-sdk` type-skew errors in `copilotAgentSession.test.ts` / `copilotToolDisplay.test.ts`

`provisional session anchors customization discovery to the additional roots (gated)` is flaky against its 2000ms timeout **on this branch's merge base** (failed 2 of 3 baseline runs); it passed 3 of 3 with these changes applied.

## Blast radius

Measured against a real `~/.copilot` with 975 SDK sessions: 492 have no Agent Host DB, of which 453 carry an extension-host marker (still gated as adoptable-legacy), leaving ~39 true externals — only 20 within the default 7-day window.

Worth flagging: a few arrive in same-second triples that look like CLI-spawned sub-sessions and will surface as separate rows. The SDK's `SessionMetadata` exposes no parent/subagent field, so there is no signal to suppress them; Claude and Codex have the same exposure today.

title: Fix typing over RTL selection requiring two keypresses
body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/monaco-editor/issues/5448

### Description of Proposed Changes
This PR resolves an input bug in the legacy `<textarea>` input pipeline (the path used when `editContext` is disabled, such as natively in Safari). 

* **The Problem:** When selecting text from right to left (RTL selection) and typing a key, the selected text is not replaced on the first keypress. A second keypress is required.
* **The Root Cause:** `TextAreaState` expects standard, normalized selection bounds (`selectionStart <= selectionEnd`). However, the `getSelectionStart()` and `getSelectionEnd()` methods in `TextAreaWrapper` were flipping these values for backward/RTL selections. This caused `selectionStart > selectionEnd` to be written and read, which violated native browser behavior (browsers automatically clamp/collapse native selections where start > end) and resulted in a state diff mismatch inside `deduceInput` (computing `replacePrevCharCnt = 1` instead of `0`).
* **The Fix:** Removed the direction-based flipping logic in `TextAreaWrapper.getSelectionStart` and `getSelectionEnd` to always return standard LTR range bounds, aligning with the expected format in `TextAreaState` and maintaining selection synchronization.

---

### How to Test
1. Open the Monaco Editor playground (or test runner) with `editContext: false` configured (or open in Safari with default options).
2. Place the cursor at the end of a line (e.g. after the semicolon in `const U = 19.05;`).
3. Press `Shift+ArrowLeft` once to select the `;` character backwards.
4. Press the `a` key once.
5. **Expected Behavior:** The selection `;` is immediately replaced with `a` on the first keypress, resulting in `const U = 19.05a`.

title: Custom Endpoint: switching an existing Chat Completions conversation to Responses API produces invalid input payload

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

body:
## Bug: Switching a conversation from Chat Completions to Responses API fails for Custom Endpoint models

### VS Code version

VS Code: 1.133.0 x64
OS: Garuda Linux x86_64 (Linux .1.8)
Copilot Chat: bundled with VS Code

### Feature

GitHub Copilot Chat → Custom Endpoint / BYOK

### Model

Custom Azure AI Foundry deployment:

gpt-5.6-luna

The model is deployed through Azure AI Foundry and supports both Chat Completions and Responses.

### Configuration

The model is configured as a custom endpoint with:

```json
{
    "id": "gpt-5.6-luna",
    "name": "Gpt 5.6 Luna",
    "url": "https://<azure-resource>/api/projects/<project>/openai/v1/responses",
    "apiType": "responses",
    "toolCalling": true,
    "vision": true,
    "maxInputTokens": 878000,
    "maxOutputTokens": 128000,
    "supportsReasoningEffort": [
        "low",
        "medium",
        "high"
    ],
    "reasoningEffortFormat": "responses",
    "streaming": true,
    "zeroDataRetentionEnabled": true
}
````

### Expected behavior

I should be able to switch from a Custom Endpoint model using the Chat Completions API to a Custom Endpoint model using the Responses API while keeping the existing conversation history.

VS Code should convert the existing conversation history into a valid Responses API `input` representation.

### Actual behavior

A fresh chat works correctly with the Responses endpoint.

However, if an existing conversation contains previous turns generated using a Chat Completions custom endpoint, switching the model to the Responses-based model fails.

The Responses request reaches Azure successfully but Azure rejects the generated historical input payload.

The first error was:

```text
400 invalid_payload

Required property 'annotations' is missing

param:
input[3].content[0].annotations
```

The same error occurred for many historical input positions:

input[3], input[5], input[10], input[12], etc.

This indicates that VS Code is generating Responses API input content from the existing Chat Completions history without including fields required by the Responses representation.

### Additional testing

I confirmed that the Azure Responses endpoint itself works independently of VS Code.

A direct request to:

```text
https://<azure-resource>/api/projects/<project>/openai/v1/responses
```

with:

```json
{
    "model": "gpt-5.6-luna",
    "input": "Hello"
}
```

returns HTTP 200.

Tool calling also works directly through the Responses endpoint.

For example, the Responses API correctly returns:

```json
{
    "type": "function_call",
    "name": "get_weather",
    "arguments": "{\"city\":\"London\"}",
    "status": "completed"
}
```

Therefore this does not appear to be an Azure/model compatibility problem.

### Important observation

When I attempted to work around the first validation error by adding:

```json
"annotations": []
```

to every `input[*].content[*]` object, Azure then returned:

```text
400 invalid_request_error

Unknown parameter:
input[0].content[0].annotations
```

This suggests that VS Code is producing a content representation that is not being correctly converted for the Responses API.

The issue appears specifically related to converting/replaying historical Chat Completions messages when the selected model uses the Responses API.

### Reproduction steps

1. Configure a Custom Endpoint Chat Completions model.
2. Start a conversation.
3. Use the model for multiple turns.
4. Allow the conversation to contain tool calls/tool results.
5. Switch the model in the same conversation to a Custom Endpoint model configured with:
   `apiType: "responses"`.
6. Send another message.
7. Observe the 400 error.

### Control test

Start a completely new conversation with the same Responses model.

Result:

SUCCESS — HTTP 200.

Therefore:

Fresh conversation → Responses model → works

Existing Chat Completions conversation → switch to Responses model → fails

### Relevant error

```text
Invalid payload: Required property 'annotations' is missing

param:
input[3].content[0].annotations
```

### Expected

VS Code should either:

1. correctly normalize the existing Chat Completions history into the Responses API input format when switching API types, or
2. prevent switching between incompatible API representations for an existing conversation and clearly indicate that a new conversation is required.

Ideally, existing conversation history should be converted automatically.

### Impact

This prevents users from switching to a stronger Responses-based reasoning model in an ongoing Agent conversation when the previous turns were generated through a Chat Completions custom endpoint.

This is particularly problematic for BYOK/custom Azure AI Foundry deployments where different models may expose different API types.

title: Respect ancestor .gitignore files in Explorer
body:
Fixes #189951

## Description

When `explorer.excludeGitIgnore` is enabled for a workspace nested inside a Git repository, Explorer currently discovers `.gitignore` files only while traversing downward from the workspace root. As a result, rules from `.gitignore` files between the workspace and repository root are never loaded.

This change:

- discovers ancestor `.gitignore` candidates up to the nearest `.git` repository boundary;
- stops ancestor discovery when the workspace is itself a repository;
- creates stable parent-chain placeholders so child negation rules continue to override ancestor rules;
- watches existing and missing ancestor `.gitignore` files for add, update, delete, and restore events;
- serializes workspace `.gitignore` processing behind ancestor initialization; and
- disposes external watches when the setting is disabled or a workspace folder is removed.

## How To Test

1. Create a Git repository with a root `.gitignore` containing `*.log`.
2. Create and open a nested folder as the VS Code workspace.
3. Enable `explorer.excludeGitIgnore`.
4. Add a `.log` file inside the workspace.
5. Confirm Explorer hides the file.
6. Add a workspace `.gitignore` containing `!keep.log` and confirm `keep.log` remains visible.
7. Update, remove, and restore an ancestor `.gitignore` and confirm Explorer refreshes without reloading the window.

## Validation

- Test-only black-box regression: fails on the unchanged baseline (`false === true`).
- Explorer browser tests: 8 passed.
- Client compilation: passed with zero errors.
- Focused ESLint: passed with zero warnings.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Manual A/B verification at the same base commit:
  - reproduced the missing ancestor rules on baseline;
  - confirmed root and intermediate ancestor rules on the fixed build;
  - confirmed child negation remains effective; and
  - confirmed live update, deletion, and restoration refresh Explorer correctly.

Only the Explorer filter implementation and its regression tests are changed.

title: multiDiffEditor: Apply the editor scrolling settings
body:
I noticed that setting `editor.mouseWheelScrollSensitivity` didn't work in the diff viewer for Git commits. This PR fixes it. :) Two older issues and a PR addressed similar problems, but were still open - I've incorporated their changes and feedback into this one as well.

The multi-file diff editor gives every per-file diff editor `handleMouseWheel: false` and sizes it to its content height, so the one scrollable that hosts all files handles the wheel. That scrollable was set up with fixed values, so four `editor.*` settings had no effect there:

- `editor.mouseWheelScrollSensitivity` and `editor.fastScrollSensitivity` fell back to the defaults in `resolveOptions`, 1 and 5.
- `editor.scrollPredominantAxis` fell back to its default, true.
- `editor.smoothScrolling` was ignored. Smooth scrolling was always on,
  while a normal editor has it off by default.

The same wheel tick that scrolls a normal editor tab by the configured amount moved the diff of a commit by the default amount instead.

Read all four settings from the configuration and keep the scrollable in sync with them. The values go through the editor option validation, so odd values behave as they do in a normal editor, and the smooth scroll duration reuses `SMOOTH_SCROLLING_TIME`.

This covers every user of the widget: the diff of a commit from the Source Control Graph, the Changes editor, and the notebook multi diff editor.

Fixes #261443
Fixes #200855

Supersedes #262669. That change covers the sensitivity settings and the predominant axis but not smooth scrolling, does not validate the values, has an unused import that fails the build, and has no tests.

title: chat: Bound external ingest reconciliation scans
body:
Fixes #328547

## Summary

- cap external-ingest workspace discovery at 100,000 raw search results across workspace folders
- preserve the existing external-ingest database and skip ingestion when discovery is truncated or fails
- expose pre-filter search limit information so regex-based Copilot exclusions cannot hide truncation
- allow a later ingest attempt to retry reconciliation

## Why

The crash dump attached to #328547 shows the workbench renderer terminating after V8 heap exhaustion while accumulating remote file-search matches. External-ingest reconciliation previously searched each workspace folder with `**/*`, `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, and no cancellation token. In a broad Remote SSH workspace, that can retain millions of search results in the renderer.

This deliberately avoids a global search cap. It only bounds external-ingest initialization and refuses to reconcile or upload from an incomplete filesystem view.

## Validation

- `npm run test:unit -- src/platform/workspaceChunkSearch/test/node/externalIngest.spec.ts` (21 passed)
- `npx tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.json` from `extensions/copilot`
- ESLint on the five changed files
- `git diff --check`

## Reviewer notes

The 100,000 limit matches the existing default local workspace-index maximum. Reaching the limit is treated conservatively as possible truncation, so external ingest is unavailable for workspaces at or above that scale until the workspace is narrowed or exclusions reduce the raw search result count. Existing database contents are preserved in that case.

(Written by Copilot)

title: Harden agent session release lifecycle
body:
## Summary

This is a lifecycle-hardening follow-up to [#330132](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/330132), which fixed [#331027](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/331027): Agent Host could release a Copilot SDK session while that session still owned a running detached shell.

The original fix correctly separated two kinds of idleness:

- AHP turn idleness: the agent loop has finished and the UI may show the session as idle.
- Provider-session releasability: detached SDK work may still be running, so the provider session must remain alive.

After that fix, review uncovered races around clients subscribing, disconnecting, and reconnecting while provider release or session restoration was asynchronous. This PR closes those gaps.

Since this PR was opened, `main` introduced `AgentHostSubscriptionService` and `AgentSessionResidency`. Those components now provide most of the original release hardening: release deduplication, provider preflight, retry after a detached-task veto or release failure, subscriber revalidation, and release-before-evict ordering. The old duplicate implementation was removed from this branch. The remaining changes cover lifecycle gaps that the refactor does not represent.

## How We Got Here

The initial detached-shell failure looked like this:

1. A chat started a shell with `mode: async` and `detach: true`.
2. The shell tool call returned immediately with a background shell ID.
3. The SDK emitted `session.idle` because the main agent loop was finished.
4. The final AHP client unsubscribed from the idle session.
5. Agent Host released the provider session after its grace period.
6. Releasing the SDK session destroyed the still-running detached shell, so its completion event and output never arrived.

[#330132](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/330132) fixed that by asking the provider whether its chats can be released and retrying later when detached work is still active.

That introduced or exposed longer asynchronous windows in the subscription lifecycle: a new subscriber may wait for a provider release to finish, or may need to restore an evicted session before its baseline snapshot is available. A client can disconnect or reconnect during either wait. This follow-up ensures those interleavings cannot leave stale ownership or corrupt client state.

## Specific Failures This Avoids

### Dead Client Permanently Pins a Session

A subscribe request can wait for an in-flight provider release or a cold session restore. If the transport disconnects during that wait, cleanup may run before `AgentService` has registered the subscriber. Without cancellation ownership:

1. disconnect cleanup removes nothing because the subscriber is not registered yet;
2. the asynchronous subscribe later resumes;
3. it registers the now-dead client ID;
4. no later path removes that subscriber;
5. `hasSessionSubscribers` remains true forever, preventing residency release and session GC.

The pending subscription record plus the `isActive` ownership predicate prevent the stale request from registering after disconnect.

### Older Subscribe Cleans Up a Newer Subscribe

Two subscribe attempts for the same client and resource can overlap around disconnect/reconnect. The older request can fail after the newer request has already become current. Cleanup must be identity-aware; otherwise the older completion can remove the newer request's subscriber registration.

### Actions Arrive Before the Baseline Snapshot

The protocol handler must remember a pending subscription so disconnect can cancel it. However, an entry in the normal subscription map is also used to decide which clients receive actions. Treating a pending entry as active can send actions before the subscribe response contains its baseline snapshot. The client then has no correct state against which to apply those actions.

State subscriptions now distinguish pending from active delivery. Pending subscriptions participate in cancellation and refcount ownership but are excluded from action routing until their baseline has resolved.

### Reconnect Delivers the Same Action Twice

Reconnect restores several channels concurrently. One channel may restore quickly while another requires a slow provider/session restore. If the fast channel becomes active immediately, an action emitted during the remaining wait can be:

1. broadcast live to the reconnecting transport; and
2. included again in the reconnect replay because its sequence is newer than the client's pre-reconnect sequence.

Many state actions are not idempotent, so applying the envelope twice can duplicate deltas or other append-style state. Successful reconnect subscriptions are activated as a batch immediately before replay is assembled.

### Snapshot Reconnect Silently Misses an Action

When the replay buffer no longer covers the client's gap, reconnect returns fresh snapshots instead of replaying actions. While subscriptions are held pending as a batch, state can still change after a fast channel's first snapshot was captured but before a slower channel finishes restoring. The final snapshot response is refreshed from authoritative state so that change is not silently omitted.

### Overlapping Transports Drop the Shared Refcount

The protocol intentionally permits an old and new transport for the same logical client to overlap during reconnect. If the old transport closes while the new transport's subscription is still pending, the pending entry must count as ownership for refcount cleanup even though it must not receive actions yet. Otherwise the old transport can remove the client ID that the reconnecting transport is in the process of retaining.

### Shutdown Continues Release Work

`AgentSessionResidency` can be inside an asynchronous provider preflight when the host shuts down. Once disposed, it must not:

- continue into provider release or cache eviction; or
- add a retry timer to its already-disposed `DisposableResourceMap`.

The residency disposal checks stop both continuations. `AgentService.unsubscribe` also avoids scheduling GC after the service has been disposed.

## Current Architecture

- `AgentHostSubscriptionService` remains the authoritative active subscriber registry.
- `AgentSessionResidency` owns release preflight, retry, deduplication, subscriber revalidation, and release-before-evict behavior.
- `ProtocolServerHandler` owns pending protocol-request identity because connection close and explicit unsubscribe occur at that layer.
- `AgentService.subscribe` accepts an ownership predicate so it can avoid registering a request that the protocol layer has already cancelled.
- Pending protocol subscriptions become active only when their baseline is ready; reconnect activation is coordinated with replay/snapshot construction.

No parallel pending-subscription registry was added to `AgentService`.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- targeted ESLint for all changed Agent Host files
- targeted `AgentService`, `AgentSessionResidency`, and `ProtocolServerHandler` suites: 511 passing, 16 pending
- pre-commit hygiene checks
- multiple Opus 5 reviews focused on correctness, necessity, and simplification

title: agentHost: Make the turn observer the only producer of turn progress
body:
Follow-up to #331045 (now merged). **Draft on purpose** — targeted for after the next release branch so it gets bake time in Insiders.

### Why

#331045 fixes a real bug but treats a symptom. The underlying problem is that reconnect runs **two** independent converters over the same response parts:

| | what it is | when it runs |
|---|---|---|
| `activeTurnToProgress` | one-shot imperative snapshot | reconnect only |
| `_observeTurn` | always-on reactive observable graph | live, reconnect, server-initiated |

Their overlap is managed by three hand-maintained continuity parameters — `adoptInvocations`, `seedEmittedLengths`, `initialResponsePartCount` — which are positional bookkeeping that must stay in sync between two converters that evolve independently. Every new response-part kind or tool status needs a matching dedup rule on the other side, and nothing enforces it.

It had already decayed in four places:

1. **A settled tool call cannot be adopted.** The snapshot renders it as `toolInvocationSerialized`, which `adoptInvocations` cannot represent, so the live graph emitted a duplicate — and that duplicate split a still-streaming response in two at the reconnect boundary.
2. **The same split for completed *subagent* tools**, which had to be exempted from the first guard so their child session would still be observed. Fixing it needed a second, separate mechanism to decouple observation from emission.
3. **`onFileEdits` was never wired on the reconnect path.** A tool completing with file edits after reconnect gets `presentation = Hidden` from `finalizeToolInvocation`, and the edit pills meant to replace it are never emitted — the card vanishes.
4. **`PendingResultConfirmation` is missing** from the `activeTurnToProgress` branch chain, so such a tool renders nothing at all on reconnect.

Items 1 and 2 are what #331045 patches, with two separate guards. Same root cause, four symptoms, and the next part kind added makes a fifth.

### What this does

Deletes the snapshot path.

`_observeTurn` is derived from state, and `autorunPerKeyedItem` runs **synchronously** on install, iterating every existing response part — so its first pass already replays the entire accumulated turn. The snapshot was recomputing what the graph produces anyway.

Reconnect is now just "install the observer", which happens before `provideChatSessionContent` returns, so `progressObs` is populated by the time the session is handed out. All three continuity parameters disappear, along with both guards from #331045, the adoption branches in the three tool-setup functions, and the cleanup that settled the orphaned snapshot invocation. `onFileEdits` is wired on the reconnect path, which the single-producer path requires (otherwise it would hit symptom 3).

`activeTurnToProgress` is no longer referenced by the handler; it stays exported for the cloud-sandbox read-only path.

**Reconnect is no longer a special case** — it is the same code path a live turn takes, so a reconnected response is indistinguishable from one watched the whole time. The invariant is structural instead of hand-maintained; there is no boundary left to get wrong. The settled-subagent case from symptom 2 needs no special handling here at all: it just falls out.

### Restore Checkpoint fix (from review)

Wiring `onFileEdits` on the reconnect path exposed an ordering problem that code review caught. The callback fires during the observer's synchronous replay, inside `provideChatSessionContent` — **before the ChatModel is created** — so `_ensureSnapshotController` found no model and `controller?.addToolCallEdits(...)` silently no-oped. Since the active turn is not in `_pendingHistoryTurns` either, edits from tools that completed before the reconnect never reached a checkpoint, leaving Restore Checkpoint without a boundary for that turn.

Those edits are now queued and flushed when the matching model appears. The pills rendered either way, so only the checkpoint data was affected.

### Risk / what to watch in Insiders

- **Rendering change:** settled tools in an active turn now render as finalized live invocations rather than serialized parts. More consistent with live turns, but it is a real change and the unit tests here are mock-driven — worth exercising a real reconnect against a long session with completed tools, file edits, terminals, and subagents.
- **Perf:** replaying a long turn now constructs live `ChatToolInvocation` objects for every completed tool instead of plain serialized objects. Same order of magnitude, but a turn with hundreds of tool calls does more work on reconnect.

### Testing

- Full `AgentHost` suite: 2210 passing. `npm run typecheck-client` clean. CI green.
- `records edits from a tool that completed before reconnect once the model appears` drives a real `AgentHostSnapshotController` and asserts `hasEditsInRequest`; verified failing before the checkpoint fix.
- Both reconnect regression tests from #331045 carry over, now asserting this branch's behavior — a finalized `toolInvocation`, which is exactly what a live turn produces for a mid-turn completion.
- Exactly one pre-existing test needed updating: `reconnecting to an active turn with owned client tool completes the initial snapshot invocation`, whose entire subject was the orphaned-snapshot workaround. With one producer there is no orphan, so it now asserts what actually matters — exactly one invocation, no duplicate.

title: agentHost: Don't split the final response at the reconnect boundary
body:
Reconnecting to an agent host session while a turn is still streaming could split the final assistant response in two — in the observed case mid-word, with the prefix folded into the collapsed tool/thinking section and the remainder rendered as a separate markdown block outside it, making it look like a tool call had interrupted the answer.

### Root cause

Reconnect runs **two** independent converters over the same response parts:

| | what it is | when it runs |
|---|---|---|
| `activeTurnToProgress` | one-shot imperative snapshot | reconnect only |
| `_observeTurn` | always-on reactive observable graph | live, reconnect, server-initiated |

They de-duplicate through `adoptInvocations`, which is keyed on live `ChatToolInvocation` instances. A tool call that had **already settled** before reconnect is rendered by the snapshot as a `toolInvocationSerialized` part, which cannot be adopted — so the live graph emitted a second, live invocation for it.

That duplicate lands *between* the restored markdown prefix and the markdown still streaming into the same response part. `ChatResponseModel` only merges a markdown update into an immediately preceding markdown part, so the two fragments stayed separate:

```
markdown prefix
tool invocation   <-- spurious
markdown continuation
```

On completion, disclosure grouped the prefix into the preceding activity section and left the continuation outside it, exposing the reconnect boundary as if it were a semantic boundary in the model's answer.

The underlying data was never wrong: the model produced one continuous response, the agent host persisted one continuous markdown part, and AHP delivered the snapshot and continuation correctly. The split was introduced entirely in the workbench.

### Fix

Record what the snapshot emitted **per tool call** rather than only the adoptable subset, so per-tool setup can skip a settled tool call that the snapshot already rendered in full. Subagent tools are excluded from the skip because their setup is what streams the child session's inner tool calls into the parent response.

This is deliberately the minimal, low-risk fix. The deeper problem is that two converters exist at all and must be kept in sync by hand; a follow-up PR removes the snapshot path entirely so reconnect and live turns share one code path. That one is riskier and wants more bake time in Insiders.

### Testing

- New regression test in the `reconnection to active turn` suite, verified failing before the change:
  ```
  + expected - actual
    [
      "toolInvocationSerialized"
      "markdown:that fallback fails to"
  -   "toolInvocation"
      "markdown:ward destroying history."
    ]
  ```

title: fix: update find searchScope when the selection changes
body:
## Description

The `searchScope` change detection in `FindReplaceState.change()` has inverted comparison logic since the multi-selection refactor in b9efdab4831 (2020): a new scope was considered *unchanged* whenever any existing scope range differed from one of the new ranges. As a result, moving or resizing the selection while Find in Selection is active kept the stale scope, and the match count never updated.

This is the root cause of the symptoms in #237774:

1. Select two lines (3 matches of the search term) → widget reports 1 result
2. Toggling Find in Selection off → highlights disappear unexpectedly
3. Changing the selection after a search → count stays at the old value

## The fix

Replace the inverted per-range comparison with a proper set-equality check (`searchScopesEqual`): same length, and every new range must be equal to some existing range. The scope is now updated whenever the selection actually changes, and no redundant change event fires when the scope is identical.

## Testing

- Added `issue #237774: Update searchScope when the selection changes` covering: moving a single selection, shrinking from two selections to one, identical scope firing no change event, and clearing the scope.
- Verified the new test fails on the previous code (stale scope kept after selection change) and passes with the fix.
- All 22 tests in `findController.test.ts` pass, including the existing multi-selection tests from #27083 and #58604 (no regression).

title: Settings Sync: conflict actions use two contradictory naming schemes, causing accidental data loss

milestone.title: Backlog
milestone.description: Work not yet planned for a specific release.

body:
## Type

Bug / UX

## Version

- VS Code: 1.130.0 (commit `1b6a188127eeaf9194f945eb6eb89a657e93c54c`, x64)
- OS: Linux 6.1.0-51-amd64 (Debian)
- Display language: German (`ms-ceintl.vscode-language-pack-de`), but the
  problem exists in the English strings as well.

## What happened

Settings Sync reported a conflict for `settings.json`. I picked the action
labelled **"Replace Local"**, expecting it to mean *"the local side is the one
to keep"* — the label leads with "Local", and the neighbouring dialog in the
same feature uses "Accept Local" to mean exactly that.

It meant the opposite. Four local settings keys were deleted and one value was
reverted to the remote state:

- `yaml.disableSchemaDetection` (6 globs) — deleted
- `git.autoRepositoryDetection` — deleted
- `githubPullRequests.experimental.chat` — deleted
- `githubPullRequests.experimental.useQuickChat` — deleted
- `git.openRepositoryInParentFolders` — reverted from `prompt` to `always`

There is no undo for this and no in-product warning that a destructive
overwrite is about to happen.

## Root cause: the same decision has two opposite naming schemes

Settings Sync labels one and the same choice in two mutually inverted ways,
depending on which surface the user happens to be on:

| Source | Key | English string |
|---|---|---|
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/userDataSync/browser/userDataSync.ts` | `replace local` | `Replace Local` |
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/userDataSync/browser/userDataSync.ts` | `replace remote` | `Replace Remote` |
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/userDataSync/browser/userDataSyncConflictsView.ts` | `acceptLocal` | `Accept Local` |
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/userDataSync/browser/userDataSyncConflictsView.ts` | `acceptRemote` | `Accept Remote` |
| `src/vs/workbench/services/userDataSync/browser/userDataSyncWorkbenchService.ts` | `replace local` | `Accept &&Remote` |
| `src/vs/workbench/services/userDataSync/browser/userDataSyncWorkbenchService.ts` | `replace remote` | `Accept &&Local` |

Note the last two rows: the internal key `replace local` renders as
**"Accept Remote"** in one place and as **"Replace Local"** in another. Both
are technically correct — replacing local *is* accepting remote — but the
user-visible words are inverted between two surfaces of the same feature.

"Replace X" names the **victim** of the operation. "Accept X" names the
**winner**. A user who has seen one scheme will systematically misread the
other, and the failure mode is silent, irreversible data loss.

## Proposal

Use one scheme everywhere, and prefer the one that names the outcome rather
than the casualty:

- **Keep Local** (local wins, remote is overwritten)
- **Keep Remote** (remote wins, local is overwritten)

"Keep X" cannot be misread the way "Replace X" can: it states what survives.
"Accept X" is an acceptable second choice — it also names the winner — but
then `Replace Local` / `Replace Remote` should be retired rather than kept
alongside it.

Optionally, add the consequence as secondary text on the destructive action,
e.g. *"Keep Remote — your local settings.json will be overwritten"*.

## Related (all closed, none covering the inconsistency itself)

- #90923 — "Replace (Overwrite Local)" button wording
- #133262 — Unclear copy for what sync settings will be replaced
- #108014 — Add "Replace Remote" to Settings Sync Turn On options
- #162884 — Settings Sync conflicts merge editor uses primary buttons

## Separate follow-up

The German localization drops the direction entirely on one of these buttons.
Filed separately as microsoft/vscode-loc#2380.

## Type

## Summary

A synchronized skill can remain advertised and resolvable by name in an active Agent Host session while its versioned plugin cache directory has already been replaced. Invoking the skill then fails with `ENOENT`, even though a newer cache version contains the same skill.

This is an independent reproduction of the general problem reported in #328464, using `create-draft-pr` rather than `act-on-feedback`. This reproduction includes the verbatim session event records and shows the affected cache version changing while the session remains active.

2. Keep the session active while synchronized customization plugin cache versions are refreshed.
3. Ask the agent to create a draft PR.
4. The agent invokes the advertised `create-draft-pr` skill.

body:
cc @anthonykim1 @meganrogge 

tl;dr
1. It seems like maybe agent host terminals are configured with shell integration differently, it's not clear whether there's a bug or it's expected
2. That caused us to enter a different branch for "cmd+up" which includes an infinite loop in old code. 

Looks like an easy fix for the hang, so I will fix that here, but please check whether there's a larger issue with how command detection is working here

---

## Summary

Pressing Cmd+Up (`workbench.action.terminal.scrollToPreviousCommand`) in an interactive Agent Host terminal can block the renderer for tens of seconds and allocate approximately 1.5 GB of JavaScript heap before the command fails.

A renderer performance trace captured a 23.3-second `keydown` handler. Approximately 92.7% of the interval was under `MarkNavigationAddon._getMarkers`, split almost entirely between `_getMarkers` and `BufferMarkCapability.markers`.

This appears to expose two separate issues.

## Issue 1: Buffer-mark navigation contains a runaway loop

`MarkNavigationAddon._getMarkers` repeatedly creates a new marker iterator:

```ts
let next = markCapability.markers().next()?.value;
const arr: IMarker[] = [];
while (next) {
	arr.push(next);
	next = markCapability.markers().next()?.value;
}
```

Because `markers()` is a generator, every call creates a fresh iterator. When at least one marker exists, every iteration reads the same first marker and appends it indefinitely. The loop only stops when array growth/allocation throws. In the captured trace, renderer heap usage reached approximately 1.51 GB before the keydown handler returned and the keybinding command rejection was surfaced through the notification service.

The direct fix is to consume one iterator, for example:

```ts
markers = [...markCapability.markers()];
```

## Issue 2: Agent Host terminals expose buffer marks without standard command detection

The Agent Host terminal manager forces shell integration, parses OSC 633 remotely, and publishes structured command-detection actions. In the renderer, `AgentHostPty` converts command boundaries into hidden `OSC 633;SetMark` sequences, which creates `TerminalCapability.BufferMarkDetection`.

However, normal visible Agent Host terminals do not expose the remote command detection as `TerminalCapability.CommandDetection`:

- `AgentHostPty.onSupportsCommandDetection` is fired but appears to have no consumer.
- `AhpTerminalCommandSource` is a separate lightweight abstraction rather than an `ICommandDetectionCapability`.
- `AhpTerminalCommandSource` is registered for hidden revived tool terminals, but not for normal interactive Agent Host terminals created by `AgentHostTerminalService.createTerminal`.

This leaves the terminal in the unusual state that triggers issue 1:

```text
BufferMarkDetection = present
CommandDetection = absent
```

The Agent Host side therefore appears to have working shell integration, but the renderer does not represent that remote capability through the normal terminal capability model. This should be investigated independently of the iterator fix, since other standard terminal features may also make incorrect decisions based on the missing capability.

## Expected behavior

1. Navigating buffer marks must terminate and must not allocate an unbounded array.
2. An interactive Agent Host terminal with remote command detection should expose an appropriate renderer-side command-detection capability, or standard terminal features should explicitly consume the AHP command source.

## Reproduction context

1. Open an interactive Agent Host terminal in the Agents Window.
2. Run at least one command so that the Agent Host publishes command-boundary marks.
3. Focus the terminal and press Cmd+Up.
4. The renderer may stop responding until the runaway allocation fails.

title: agentHost: fix resuming sessions with deleted worktrees
body:
## Summary

Fixes #331030.

Archived worktree sessions are read-only, and archiving deliberately removes their worktree after preserving the branch and source-repository metadata. When an archived session is reopened, the Copilot SDK still requires an existing working directory in order to load its transcript. The intended behavior is therefore to resume the SDK against the source repository for history only, rather than recreate the archived worktree.

## What went wrong

Copilot sessions can have two different identities:

- The **Agent Host configuration/session ID**, which owns working-directory metadata and customizations.
- The **Copilot SDK session ID**, which identifies the persisted SDK conversation.

When those IDs are equal, restoration uses `_resumeSession` / `_doResumeSession`. That path already calls `resolveWorkingDirectoryForResume` before constructing the SDK launch plan.

When the IDs differ, restoration uses `_resolveOrResumeChatSession` for the exact persisted chat backing. Modern default chats can use this path—not only additional or peer chats. This path previously passed the deleted worktree directly to `client.resumeSession`, bypassing the existing resolver and producing:

> Request session.resume failed with message: Directory does not exist or cannot be accessed: /path/to/removed/worktree

## Fix

Route the divergent-backing path through `IAgentConfigurationService.resolveWorkingDirectoryForResume` too.

The resolver does not change the process cwd. It returns the safe directory that should be supplied to the resumed SDK session:

- If the persisted directory still exists, return it unchanged.
- If it is missing and the session is archived, return the persisted source-repository root so the read-only transcript can load.
- If it is missing and the session is live, recreate the preserved worktree and return that path; never silently run an interactive session in the source repository.
- If no safe directory can be recovered, surface `SessionWorkingDirectoryMissingError`.

The resolved directory is then used consistently for the SDK launch plan, shell manager, and customization discovery.

For multi-root sessions, the change replaces only index 0 (the deleted primary worktree) with the resolved directory, preserves secondary roots, and persists the corrected ordered root set. This prevents the next restore from reading a stale primary path from `copilot.workingDirectories`.

## Tests

- Added regression coverage for a default chat whose Agent Host ID differs from its Copilot SDK backing ID.
- Verifies that the resolved repository is used as the launch/customization directory.
- Verifies that secondary roots are preserved.
- Verifies that the corrected root set is persisted.

body:
cc @DonJayamanne possibly from multi-root stuff, but seems like an easy fix

## Type of issue

Bug

## Reproduction

1. Create an Agent Host Copilot session using worktree isolation.
2. Archive the session, allowing archive cleanup to remove its worktree.
3. Reopen the archived session when its Agent Host session ID differs from its persisted Copilot SDK backing ID.

## Actual behavior

The session fails to open with an error like:

> Request session.resume failed with message: Directory does not exist or cannot be accessed: /path/to/removed/worktree

## Expected behavior

Archived sessions are read-only and should resume against the persisted source repository when their worktree has been removed, so their history remains accessible.

## Cause

There are two Copilot resume paths:

- `_resumeSession` / `_doResumeSession` handles sessions whose Agent Host configuration ID is also the Copilot SDK session ID. This path calls `resolveWorkingDirectoryForResume`, which falls back to the repository root for archived sessions.
- `_resolveOrResumeChatSession` handles persisted chat backings whose Copilot SDK session ID differs from the Agent Host configuration ID. This path currently passes the persisted working directory directly to the SDK without resolving it first.

Modern default chats can use the second path, not just additional/peer chats. Consequently, an archived default chat with a divergent SDK backing ID bypasses the existing missing-worktree fallback.

## Proposed fix

Resolve the persisted working directory through `IAgentConfigurationService.resolveWorkingDirectoryForResume` in `_resolveOrResumeChatSession` before creating the active client, shell manager, and resume launch plan. Reanchor customization discovery to the resolved directory as `_doResumeSession` does.

Add regression coverage for a divergent persisted backing whose missing archived worktree resolves to its source repository.

The duplicated resume orchestration between `_doResumeSession` and `_resolveOrResumeChatSession` is also a maintenance hazard and could be consolidated separately.

(Written by Copilot)

body:
## Type of issue

Bug

## Reproduction

This reproduces on macOS with a Copilot CLI session running through Agent Host. The detached command must run longer than the Agent Host idle-release grace period (currently 30 seconds).

1. Open VS Code Insiders and open a folder in an Agent Host-backed Copilot CLI chat session.
2. Send this prompt to the agent:

   ```text
   Use the bash tool with mode `async`, `detach: true`, and `initial_wait: 30` to run this command:

   node -e "setTimeout(() => require('fs').writeFileSync('/tmp/vscode-agent-host-detached-shell-repro', 'done'), 120000)"

   After the tool reports that the command started in the detached background, end the turn immediately. Do not call read_bash or wait for the command.
   ```

3. Confirm that the shell tool reports something similar to:

   ```text
   <command started in detached background with shellId: ...>
   ```

4. Wait for the chat session to become idle.
5. Navigate to another chat/session or close the chat so that the original session no longer has a subscribed client.
6. After navigating away, wait 130 seconds without reopening the session. This gives Agent Host time to release the idle session and gives the detached command time to finish if it survived.
7. Check whether the marker file was created:

   ```bash
   cat /tmp/vscode-agent-host-detached-shell-repro
   ```

8. Reopen the original chat and check for the detached-shell completion notification.

## Expected behavior

The AHP turn and session may become idle, but the detached shell continues running independently. Agent Host must not release/disconnect the provider session while the SDK still reports a running detached shell. After approximately two minutes:

- `/tmp/vscode-agent-host-detached-shell-repro` contains `done`;
- the session receives the detached-shell completion notification; and
- the agent can retrieve the completed shell output.

## Actual behavior

After the session becomes idle and loses its last subscriber, Agent Host releases the session after the grace period. Releasing the Copilot SDK session destroys the outstanding detached shell. The marker file is never created and no completion notification arrives.

The initial `session.idle` event is expected for detached work: detached shells are not part of the active agent loop. The bug is treating agent-loop idleness as sufficient to release the provider session.

## Lifecycle evidence

In the original report:

1. Two commands started with `mode: async` and `detach: true`.
2. Both tool calls completed immediately with detached shell IDs.
3. The SDK emitted `session.idle`, and AHP correctly completed the active turn.
4. One detached shell completed before eviction, proving that detached work survives the initial idle transition.
5. The other shell was still running when the final client unsubscribed.
6. Agent Host logged `Evicting idle session` and `Releasing idle session from memory`.
7. The SDK emitted `session.shutdown` and destroyed the session.
8. The remaining detached shell never emitted `shell_detached_completed`.

The SDK exposes authoritative detached-task state through `session.rpc.tasks.refresh()` and `session.rpc.tasks.list()`. A running detached shell is represented as a shell task with `attachmentMode: detached` and status `running` or `idle`.

## Proposed behavior / fix

Before idle eviction tears down provider resources, ask the provider whether each chat can release its in-memory backing. For Copilot, refresh/list SDK tasks and defer release while a detached shell is still running. Keep AHP state idle; only provider eviction is deferred. Retry release after the normal grace period.

Draft fix: [#330132](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/330132)

(Written by Copilot)

title: Keep the expected managed settings 404 out of the DevTools console
body:
### Problem

Developer Tools logs this repeatedly, and it looks like a failure:

```
api.github.com/copilot_internal/managed_settings:1  Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 ()
```

The `404` is not a problem — it is how the endpoint says "this account has no managed settings", and `DefaultAccountProvider` already handles it as a normal outcome. The problem is purely that it gets printed.

### Why it can't be fixed in the renderer

Chromium emits that line from the document's network stack for any response with an error status. Measured via the DevTools `Log` domain (`Log.entryAdded`, which is exactly what the console renders):

| request from the renderer | printed? |
|---|---|
| `fetch` | yes |
| `XMLHttpRequest` | yes |
| `fetch` + `keepalive` / `cache: 'no-store'` | yes |
| same, inside an iframe | yes |

There is no request option that suppresses it, and it is not a `console.*` call that could be filtered.

### Fix

Rewrite the status in the main process before the response reaches the window, using the same `session.defaultSession.webRequest.onHeadersReceived` mechanism that already sits a few lines above in `app.ts` (used to add `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` for the PRSS CDN). The real status travels in a response header that the workbench restores immediately, so **every downstream code path still sees the `404` it sees today** — including the retry-next-session logic and the `noSettings` handling.

Scope is deliberately tight: only a `404`, only from `https://api.*/copilot_internal/managed_settings` (covering GHES, whose host is also `api.`-prefixed). Any other status, endpoint or genuine failure is reported exactly as before.

One subtlety worth flagging for review: the request is cross-origin, so the marker header is invisible to the window unless it is added to `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`. That list is *extended*, not replaced — replacing it would hide the `x-ratelimit-remaining` / `retry-after` headers that the rate-limit logic reads off this same response.

### Verification

Ran the shipped predicate and handler verbatim in Electron (the `.build/electron` binary this repo uses), against a real `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/managed_settings?client_id=…` URL served by a local HTTPS endpoint that mimics GitHub's response (CORS, its own `access-control-expose-headers`, `x-ratelimit-remaining`), with the DevTools `Log` domain attached:

```
managed_settings (real URL + query)
   renderer: {"status":200,"original":"404","rateLimit":"4999","body":"{\"message\":\"Not Found\"}"}
   console : silent
other copilot endpoint (untouched)
   renderer: {"status":404,"original":null,"rateLimit":"4999","body":"{\"message\":\"Not Found\"}"}
   console : PRINTS -> Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)
```

So: the noise is gone, the true status is recovered, the rate-limit headers survive, and neighbouring endpoints are unaffected.

Also: `scripts/test.sh` on the three related suites (53 passing, including new unit tests for the URL predicate and the status restore), plus `tsc -p src/tsconfig.json`, `eslint`, and `valid-layers-check`.

### Notes

- Desktop only. The web workbench still prints it; that would need the service to stop answering `404`.
- While investigating I found a separate, unrelated inefficiency: `findMatchingProviderSession` lists one session once per scope set it matches, so a full-scope GitHub session is listed 3× and the identical request is sent 3× with the same token. That is a real bug but it is *not* the cause of the printing, so I have left it out of this PR — happy to send it separately.

title: Built-in SQL language mode is displayed as "MS SQL", even though it's generic and dialect-agnostic
body:
## Description

VS Code's built-in "SQL Language Basics" extension (`vscode.sql`) registers the `sql` language ID with the display name **"MS SQL"**. This is misleading: the grammar is purely generic syntax highlighting (keywords, brackets), with no connection to Microsoft SQL Server / T-SQL specifically. It's applied by default to *every* `.sql` file, regardless of actual dialect.

I ran into this while editing PostgreSQL migration files — the status bar and language-mode picker both show "MS SQL" for a file that uses plain PostgreSQL syntax (`jsonb`, `->>`, `generated always as (...) stored`), none of which are T-SQL constructs. This is confusing: it strongly implies the file is being treated as, or should be treated as, Microsoft SQL Server syntax, when in fact the language mode does nothing dialect-specific at all.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ensure no SQL-dialect-specific extensions (e.g. `mssql`, `SQLTools`) are installed — only the built-in "SQL Language Basics".
2. Create a `.sql` file containing PostgreSQL-only syntax, e.g.:
   ```sql
   create table example (
     data jsonb,
     valid boolean generated always as (
       (data->>'valid')::boolean
     ) stored
   );
   ```
3. Open the file in VS Code.
4. Look at the language mode indicator in the bottom-right status bar, or open the language picker (click the indicator, or "Select Language Mode").

## Expected

The status bar / language picker shows a name that reflects the generic, dialect-agnostic nature of the built-in grammar — e.g. "SQL".

## Actual

It shows "MS SQL", despite the file containing no Microsoft SQL Server-specific syntax, and despite no mssql-related extension being installed. Confirmed via the extension's own "Feature Contributions" tab: ID: sql, Name: MS SQL, File Extensions: .sql, .dsql.

## Suggested fix

Rename the built-in sql language's display name from "MS SQL" to "SQL", to match its actual (generic) behavior.

## Details

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes — the built-in "SQL Language Basics" extension is itself the source, and is not affected by "disable all extensions" / --disable-extensions, since it's a built-in, not a marketplace extension.

title: agentHost: Add agent merge controller
body:
## Summary

Adds a provider-neutral Agent Merge controller to the Agent Host so Copilot, Codex, and Claude can maintain a pull request through the same lifecycle.

- watches the session pull request through the shared GitHub API service
- deterministically gates review feedback, required CI failures, conflicts, and merge readiness before starting a model turn
- gives repair turns narrowly scoped GitHub tools for CI diagnostics, review-thread replies, and workflow reruns
- performs final direct merges and merge-queue enrollment in native Agent Host code rather than delegating them to the model
- persists per-session enablement, pull request binding, action overrides, watermarks, attempt budgets, and injected permission-mode state across restores
- adds experimental `chat.agentHost.agentMerge.*` settings and Agents Window commands to enable, disable, or configure the active session
- adds structured `ILogService` diagnostics without logging prompts, comment bodies, CI logs, credentials, or local paths

## Behavior and safety

Agent Merge fails closed when GitHub state is incomplete, does not create turns while required checks are pending, and only treats feedback from repository owners, members, collaborators, or the Copilot pull request reviewer as actionable. The agent is never authorized to merge. A fresh native readiness check runs immediately before direct merge or queue enrollment.

Enabling Agent Merge switches the session to Autopilot mode and Assisted approvals unless managed policy forbids elevated approval modes. Disabling restores values only when they still match the injected values, preserving later manual changes. Branch or pull request identity changes disable the controller and require explicit re-enablement.

The initial VS Code surface is intentionally command-only; no dedicated status UI is included yet.

- `npm run valid-layers-check`

title: Settle Copilot WebSocket requests when `error` is not followed by `close`
body:
Fixes #331003

## Description

An active Copilot Responses API WebSocket request currently settles connection failures from the socket `close` listener. The `error` listener only stores `_pendingErrorMessage` for that later close.

Observed Electron failures can emit `error` without a subsequent `close`. In that case `handle.firstEvent` and `handle.done` remain pending indefinitely, which also prevents the existing HTTP retry path from running.

This change settles the active request immediately on `error`, marks the connection closed, and closes the socket. A focused regression simulates an error with no close event and verifies both promises reject.

title: Copilot agent request can hang when WebSocket emits `error` without `close`
body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.61.0
- VS Code Version: 1.133.0
- OS Version: Windows 11 Enterprise, build 26200
- Feature: Agent mode
- Selected model: Not captured in the sanitized occurrence record
- Logs: Sanitized signature and state transition below; no prompts or responses included

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a long-running Copilot agent request using a model whose metadata enables the Responses API WebSocket endpoint.
2. While an active request is awaiting `handle.firstEvent` / `handle.done`, cause the Electron WebSocket to emit an `error` event without a subsequent `close` event. The linked PR's unit test reproduces this deterministically with `FakeWebSocket.simulateError()` and no close.
3. Observe that the agent remains pending until the user presses Stop or Retry.

## Expected

An active-socket error should settle the request immediately. The existing request-error path can then retry over HTTP when eligible, or show a terminal error to the user.

## Actual

`ChatWebSocketConnection` records the error in `_pendingErrorMessage`, but only calls `handleConnectionClose` from the socket `close` listener. If no close event follows, both `firstEvent` and `done` remain pending, so the request has no terminal transition and HTTP fallback never starts.

Observed log signature:

```text
[ChatWebSocketManager] Error for conversation <conversation-id> turn <request-id>: :
```

No matching later line was present for the same conversation and turn:

```text
[ChatWebSocketManager] Connection closed for conversation <conversation-id> turn <request-id> ...
```

After manual intervention, persisted state showed:

```text
native status: idle (1)
lastResponseState: 2
transport failure: chat-websocket-error
```

This occurred in five conversations in one extension host on the same day. One affected conversation reproduced the signature again while the investigation was running. Tool executions had completed; the silent interval began after a tool/sub-turn, not inside a terminal command.

## Root Cause

In `extensions/copilot/src/platform/networking/node/chatWebSocketManager.ts`, the active-socket `error` handler only stores `_pendingErrorMessage`. Request settlement occurs in the independent `close` handler. The implementation assumes every error is followed by close, which is not guaranteed by the observed Electron transport behavior.

## Proposed Fix

On an active-socket error:

1. Mark the connection closed.
2. Clear the active request from the connection.
3. Settle it through `handleConnectionClose(1006, '', errorMessage)`.
4. Close the underlying socket.

The linked PR's regression emits `error` without `close` and verifies `firstEvent` and `done` reject and the connection closes.

- Implementation patch applied: all 24 tests in `chatWebSocketManager.spec.ts` passed.
- `npm run typecheck`: passed.
- `npm run lint`: passed with zero warnings.
- TypeScript language diagnostics and `git diff --check`: clean.

Potentially related but not duplicate: #314336 and #329550. Neither public report identifies the error-without-close state-machine path.

title: Custom agent `agents:` frontmatter allowlist is parsed but never enforced by RunSubagentTool — coordinator can invoke any enabled agent, not just the ones listed

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

body: ## Requirements - Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): agent mode, custom agent with `agents:` frontmatter delegating via the `agent` tool (`runSubagent`) - Selected model: Local/BYOK model (Qwen 3.8-27B) — noted for completeness, but the underlying issue is in `runSubagent`'s dispatch logic and isn't model-specific ## Summary A custom agent's `agents:` frontmatter field is documented as an allowlist restricting which subagents a coordinator can delegate to (see [vscode-docs/docs/agents/subagents.md](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-docs/blob/main/docs/agents/subagents.md): "You can restrict which custom agents can be used as subagents by specifying the `agents` property in the main agent's frontmatter, and providing a list of allowed custom agents."). In practice, the allowlist is parsed but never checked before dispatch. A coordinator agent with `agents: ['A', 'B']` can still successfully invoke any other enabled, non-`disable-model-invocation` custom agent in the workspace by name — the `agents:` list has no effect on what `runSubagent` will actually execute. ## Steps to Reproduce Observed in the wild with a real orchestrator agent, then isolated to a minimal case below. **As observed:** A coordinator agent (`agents: ["Test Case", "Executor", "Plan"]` in frontmatter, body text referring to delegating to a "TDD"/"Test Case" subagent for Phase 1) was given a task and, unprompted, opened a subagent step labeled "Orchestrator: Research Tuff codebase" — invoking something outside its own `agents:` list before Phase 1 even began. See attached screenshot (`orchestrator-research-screenshot.png`): the response reads "I'll start by understanding the Tuff codebase and how this test case fits in, then run the orchestrator phases. Let me first research the project," followed by a collapsed subagent invocation titled "Orchestrator: Research Tuff codebase." No agent named "Research" (or anything matching that label) appears anywhere in the coordinator's `agents:` allowlist. **Minimal isolation (not yet independently re-verified — please confirm on your end before triaging further):** 1. Create a coordinator agent, e.g. `.github/agents/coordinator.agent.md`: ```yaml --- name: Coordinator tools: ['agent'] agents: ['Allowed'] --- You orchestrate work. You must only ever delegate to the Allowed agent. ``` 2. Create two more agents in the same folder: - `.github/agents/allowed.agent.md` with `name: Allowed` - `.github/agents/forbidden.agent.md` with `name: Forbidden` (no `disable-model-invocation`, so it remains available as a subagent by default) 3. In chat, select the Coordinator agent and send a prompt that explicitly asks it to invoke the Forbidden agent, e.g.: `Use the runSubagent tool to invoke the agent named "Forbidden" and ask it to say hello.` 4. Observe that the `runSubagent` tool call succeeds and Forbidden actually runs, despite not being present in Coordinator's `agents: ['Allowed']` list. ## Expected Behavior `runSubagent` should reject (or the model should be prevented from even attempting) delegation to any custom agent not present in the calling agent's `agents:` list, matching the documented allowlist behavior. ## Actual Behavior `runSubagent` dispatches to any enabled custom agent found by name, regardless of the calling agent's `agents:` list. ## Root Cause (source reference) Looked through `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/tools/builtinTools/runSubagentTool.ts` on `main`: - `IChatRequestModeInstructions` (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/model/chatModel.ts`) has a field `readonly allowedSubagents?: readonly string[]` that appears to exist specifically for this purpose. - `chatInputPart.ts` populates it once, from `mode.agents?.get()`, when a mode is selected at the top level of the chat input. - However, in `RunSubagentTool.invoke()`, the name lookup goes straight to: ```ts private async getSubAgentByName(name: string): Promise { const agents = await this.promptsService.getCustomAgents(CancellationToken.None); return agents.find(agent => agent.name === name && agent.enabled); } ``` This searches every registered custom agent in the workspace by name and `enabled` status only — it never consults `currentModeInstructions.allowedSubagents` (or the equivalent `agents:` list) before returning a match. - When building `modeInstructions` for the newly-dispatched subagent, `allowedSubagents` is explicitly discarded: ```ts modeInstructions = instructions && { name: subAgentName, content: instructions.content, toolReferences: this.languageModelToolsService.toToolReferences(instructions.toolReferences), allowedSubagents: undefined, // always undefined here metadata: instructions.metadata, isBuiltin: isBuiltinAgent(subagent.source, subagent.uri, this.productService), }; ``` - Searching the whole file, `currentModeInstructions?.allowedSubagents` (or any equivalent check against the calling agent's own `agents:` list) is never read anywhere in `invoke()` or `prepareToolInvocation()` before a subagent is actually dispatched. The only place `allowedSubagents` is written is `chatInputPart.ts`; the only places it's set are the two spots above (one from `mode.agents`, one hardcoded `undefined`) — there is no read site that gates dispatch. Net effect: the `agents:` field currently functions as documentation/UI hinting only, not as an enforced security or scoping boundary. ## Why this matters Multi-agent orchestration patterns rely on this allowlist to keep a coordinator from silently substituting an unintended agent when names or descriptions are similar — the docs call this out directly as the reason the field exists. Right now that protection doesn't fire, so a coordinator can (and in my testing, did) invoke an agent outside its stated `agents:` list without any error, warning, or indication that the allowlist was bypassed. ## Suggested fix direction In `RunSubagentTool.invoke()` (and ideally `prepareToolInvocation()` so it can fail fast / show a clear tool-prep error), before calling `getSubAgentByName`, check the requested `subAgentName` against `currentModeInstructions?.allowedSubagents` when that list is defined and non-empty, and reject with a clear error (similar to the existing "Requested agent '...' not found" error) if the name isn't present. Separately, `allowedSubagents: undefined` on the newly constructed `modeInstructions` for the dispatched subagent should presumably be populated from that subagent's own `agents:` frontmatter (`subagent.agents`), so nested delegation continues to respect each agent's own allowlist rather than losing it on every hop. *Disclaimer: Issue text generated by Sonnet 5, but issue has been confirmed and repeated by a human.*

title: Copilot read_file truncation can split UTF-16 surrogate pairs and poison a chat session

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: verified
labels.description: Verification succeeded

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.61.0
- VS Code Version: 1.133.0
- OS Version: Windows
- Feature: Agent mode
- Selected model: GPT-5.6 Sol
- Logs: filtered synthetic excerpt in the attached clean-reproduction ZIP; identifiers removed

## Summary

The built-in Copilot `read_file` tool truncates lines with JavaScript `slice(0, 2000)`. If an astral Unicode character crosses that UTF-16 boundary, the tool result retains only the high surrogate. The malformed result is persisted in the chat session and included in subsequent requests. Both WebSocket and fallback HTTP then fail with `400 invalid_request_body`, and Retry cannot recover because it resends the same poisoned context.

The source appears to be:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/extensions/copilot/src/extension/tools/node/readFileTool.tsx

```ts
const MAX_LINE_LENGTH = 2000;

let contents = rawContents.split('\n').map(line => {
    if (line.length > MAX_LINE_LENGTH) {
        hadLongLines = true;
        return line.slice(0, MAX_LINE_LENGTH) + ' [truncated]';
    }
    return line;
}).join('\n');
```

## Minimal reproduction

The string operation itself is deterministic:

```js
const max = 2000;
const line = 'x'.repeat(max - 1) + '\u{1F6E1}' + 'tail';
const result = line.slice(0, max) + ' [truncated]';

console.log(JSON.stringify(result));
// Ends with: ...xxxxxxxx\ud83d [truncated]"
```

End-to-end reproduction using the attached `clean-repro` folder:

1. Run `node .\generate-repro-fixture.mjs` to create a valid UTF-8 fixture containing 1,999 ASCII characters, then `U+1F6E1`, then an ASCII tail.
2. Open the folder in a new VS Code window and start a fresh GPT-5.6 Sol agent chat.
3. Prompt: `This is a synthetic Unicode regression test. Use only read_file to read surrogate-boundary.txt from line 1 through line 1. Do not use terminal or other tools. After reading it, reply exactly FIRST_TURN_COMPLETE.`
4. Observe that the initial model step succeeds and invokes only `read_file`.
5. Observe that the immediate continuation fails with WebSocket `invalid_json`, a successful CAPI connectivity ping, and fallback HTTP `400 invalid_request_body`. The requested response is never emitted.

No second user prompt is needed; the failure occurs within this first turn when the model continues after the tool result.

## Actual result

The synthetic fixture is valid UTF-8 and contains no unpaired surrogates. Its `U+1F6E1` occupies UTF-16 indexes 1,999 and 2,000. The fresh chat ledger is valid JSON syntax but its persisted `read_file` result contains exactly one unpaired `U+D83D` at zero-based index 1,999, immediately followed by ` [truncated]`.

Representative extension-host log sequence:

```text
WebSocket CAPI error: [invalid_json] Invalid websocket message: failed to parse JSON value
CAPI ping successful, proceeding with chat request retry
Server error: 400 {"error":{"message":"Invalid body: failed to parse JSON value...","code":"invalid_request_body"}}
[ToolCallingLoop] Auto-retrying on error (attempt 1/3)
```

The attached `vscode-readfile-surrogate-clean-repro-20260814.zip` contains only public-safe synthetic evidence:

- `README.md`: reproduction instructions and exact prompt.
- `generate-repro-fixture.mjs`: deterministic fixture generator.
- `surrogate-boundary.txt`: generated valid UTF-8 fixture.
- `synthetic-extension.log`: filtered extension-host sequence with request IDs and UUIDs redacted.
- `session-structure.json`: content-blind structural scan proving `read_file` was the only tool and locating the lone surrogate.
- `extract-sanitized-log.ps1`: the exact event filter and redaction script.

The raw chat ledger and raw extension-host log are intentionally not attached.

## Expected result

- `read_file` truncation never splits a surrogate pair.
- Persisted tool results and outbound request bodies contain valid Unicode.
- Deterministic `400 invalid_request_body` errors are not retried multiple times with an unchanged body.
- If legacy persisted state contains an unpaired surrogate, Copilot either repairs it with `U+FFFD` or identifies the bad session and offers a clear recovery path.

## Proposed root fix

Before slicing at `MAX_LINE_LENGTH`, move the end index back by one when the boundary falls between a high and low surrogate. Add a unit test whose emoji begins at index 1,999.

This preserves the existing 2,000 UTF-16-unit cap while ensuring the result is well formed.

## Fix validation

Validated against the exact `@vscode/copilot-api` 0.5.2 lock:

- the focused regression test fails before the production fix and all 35 focused tests pass after it;
- typecheck and compile pass;
- the full Copilot unit suite passes (8,915 tests, with 129 skipped);
- the patched extension completes the synthetic GPT-5.6 Sol turn with `FIRST_TURN_COMPLETE`;
- a content-blind scan finds one `read_file` marker, no malformed JSON lines, no unpaired surrogates, and no WebSocket/JSON/400/retry failure signatures.

An exact cause-focused metadata search of `microsoft/vscode` issues was repeated on 2026-08-14. No issue title or exact query matched `read_file` splitting a surrogate pair, persisting an unpaired surrogate, or causing the resulting JSON failures. The broader results included #253136, a generic Copilot request-failure tracker, and #321578, titled "read_file reads only 2000 characters"; neither metadata result describes this surrogate-boundary corruption.

## Related but distinct prior art

https://github.com/github/copilot-sdk/pull/2283 repairs unpaired UTF-16 surrogate escapes in incoming Rust JSON-RPC frames. That is the same failure class but a different boundary. This issue is produced locally by VS Code's `read_file` line truncation and later fails on outbound CAPI request construction/parsing.

A defense-in-depth outbound/session sanitizer would be useful, but it should accompany rather than replace the producer fix.

# HTML language service does not report unmatched or invalid closing tags Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: **Yes** * VS Code Version: 1.133.0 (System setup) * OS Version: Windows 11 25H2 ### Steps to Reproduce: 1. Create a new `.html` file. 2. Add the following markup: ```html id="e9qzv7"
  • Services
    • Ship agency
    • Ship management
    • Consulation
    • Technical management
    • Bunker supply
    • Ship Chartering & brokering
    • Ship supply
    • ``` 3. Open the **Problems** panel. ### Actual Behavior No diagnostic is reported for the malformed HTML structure. There are at least two obvious structural errors: 1. `` is an unexpected/unmatched closing tag: ```html id="4prz7k" Services ^^^^ ``` 2. The closing `` tag incorrectly contains an attribute: ```html id="qg1h8j" ^^^^^^^^^^^^^ ``` The Problems panel remains empty for these errors when using VS Code's built-in HTML language support. ### Expected Behavior The built-in HTML language service should report diagnostics for basic malformed HTML structure, including: * unexpected/unmatched closing tags; * mismatched opening and closing tags; * invalid attributes on closing tags. For example, an unexpected `` should be reported as an error or warning at the location of the invalid closing tag. ### Additional Information The issue reproduces with **all extensions disabled**, so this does not appear to be caused by an extension. I am not requesting full W3C/WHATWG validation here. The request is specifically for basic structural HTML diagnostics. A third-party HTML linter such as HTMLHint is currently required to catch some of these issues, while VS Code's built-in HTML language service does not report them. It would be useful if the built-in HTML language service could provide diagnostics for these basic structural errors directly in the **Problems** panel.
