title: Harden launch skill TMPDIR fallback
body:
Fixes the review comments from https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/330988.

- **Atomic run directory.** That PR's `/tmp` fallback created the run dir at a predictable path in a world-writable directory, where another local user could pre-create or symlink it ahead of `mkdir -p`. The run dir is now always created with `mktemp -d`, which is atomic and `0700` regardless of `TMPDIR`.
- **Byte-based length check.** `${#RUN_DIR}` counts characters while the socket limit is bytes, so a multibyte `TMPDIR` could pass the check and still fail with `EINVAL`. A 59-char / 79-byte path reproduces this; now measured with `printf | wc -c`.
- **Corrected `EINVAL` troubleshooting tip.** The socket path is `TMPDIR` plus playwright's own prefix plus the `-s=` session name, which leaves about 16 characters for the session name on macOS defaults - so the previous advice to `export TMPDIR=/tmp` was both inaccurate and unnecessary.

Verified end-to-end on macOS with both the default `TMPDIR` and `TMPDIR=/tmp`: each reaches `CDP ready` with a `drwx------` run dir.

title: Fix launch skill on macOS default TMPDIR
body: macOS's default `TMPDIR` pushed the Electron IPC socket path past the ~103-char unix socket limit, failing every launch with `EINVAL`. Falls back to `/tmp`, and documents the same limit for the Playwright daemon.

title: Editor patch tool bypasses agent sandbox write allowlist

labels.name: info-needed
labels.description: Issue requires more information from poster

body:
### Summary
A Copilot agent session whose sandbox policy allowed writes only to the workspace and system temp directory successfully wrote a file directly into the user’s home directory using the editor-level patch tool.

### Sandbox policy
- **Workspace:** `D:\Dev\.github-private`
- **Allowed read/write paths:**
  - `D:\Dev\.github-private`
  - `C:\Users\haral\AppData\Local\Temp`
- **Denied paths:** none explicitly listed
- **Network:** outbound blocked

### Reproduction
1. Start an agent session in `D:\Dev\.github-private`.
2. Confirm the effective sandbox policy has the two read/write paths above.
3. Ask the agent to create a simple “hello world” file in the user home directory.
4. The agent invokes the editor patch tool with an absolute path:
   ```text
   C:\Users\haral\hello-world.txt
   ```
5. The tool reports success, and the file exists with the expected contents:
   ```text
   Hello, World!
   ```

### Expected behavior
All agent write mechanisms, including editor-integrated patch/edit tools, should enforce the same sandbox write allowlist. An attempt to write `C:\Users\haral\hello-world.txt` should be rejected.

### Actual behavior
The patch tool created the file outside the permitted paths, suggesting editor-level file operations are not subject to the same write restrictions as sandboxed shell commands.

### Impact
An agent can modify arbitrary user-writable files outside the workspace despite an effective sandbox policy intended to restrict writes to the workspace and temp directory.

title: Use refresh token for XAA when available
body:
For #316625

## Summary

In the XAA (Cross App Access / Enterprise Managed Auth) flow, VS Code bootstraps an IdP session with the `openid offline_access` scopes, obtaining both an ID token and a refresh token. Previously, only the ID Token was used as the `subject_token` in the RFC 8693 token exchange that mints an ID-JAG (leg 2). Because ID tokens are short-lived (typically 1 hour), any attempt to silently obtain an access token for an MCP server after the ID token expired would fail, even though a long-lived refresh token was already in storage and never used.

This PR changes the subject token preference:

- Prefer refresh token when one is available in the stored IdP session. Refresh tokens are long-lived and do not have the expiry problem.
- Fall back to ID token for IdPs that do not issue a refresh token (e.g. when `offline_access` is refused).

## Changes

- `oauth.ts`: Adds `TOKEN_TYPE_REFRESH_TOKEN` constant. Generalises `buildIdJagExchangeBody` to accept explicit `subjectToken` / `subjectTokenType` parameters instead of hardcoding ID token.
- `extHostAuthentication.ts`: Widens `_tokenStore` visibility from private to protected so the XAA mixin can look up raw tokens (including refresh token) by access_token.
- `extHostXaaAuthProvider.ts`: Adds `_hasSubjectToken()` helper. Updates `_mintResourceToken` to resolve the subject token — looking up the raw `IAuthorizationToken` from the store and preferring refresh token when present. Updates the early guards in `getSessions` and `createSession` to accept either token type.
- `oauth.test.ts`: Updates existing `buildIdJagExchangeBody` call sites to pass the explicit token type argument; adds a new test case for the refresh token subject type.

## Testing

1. Sign in to an IdP that issues refresh tokens with `offline_access` — confirm the token exchange request sends `subject_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:refresh_token`.
2. Wait for / simulate an expired ID token in the stored session — confirm silent re-mint succeeds without prompting the user.
3. Sign in to an IdP that does not issue a refresh token — confirm the flow falls back to ID token and behaves as before.
